q: How is ethanoic acid made in vinegar production?
options: Ethene is hydrated using steam and an acid catalyst.
Bacteria oxidise ethanol using oxygen from the air.
Ethanol is cracked at high temperature.
explain: In vinegar production bacteria oxidise ethanol in dilute alcoholic drinks such as wine to ethanoic acid.

q: Which pair of monomers forms a polyester?
options: a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine
a dicarboxylic acid and a diol
explain: A polyester forms when a dicarboxylic acid reacts with a diol. The ester links form with loss of water.

q: Ethene reacts with steam at 300 °C and 60 atm. What is the structural formula of the product?
explain: Steam adds across the C=C bond in the presence of an acid catalyst to make ethanol.

q: Why is the molecular formula C₂H₆O not an unambiguous description of ethanol?
options: It does not show how the atoms are arranged, so it could also be CH₃OCH₃.
It does not show the number of carbon atoms in the molecule.
It does not show which elements are present in the molecule.
It shows the compound as an ionic substance.
explain: A molecular formula gives only the atoms present. CH₃CH₂OH and CH₃OCH₃ share the formula C₂H₆O, so the structural formula is needed to be unambiguous.

q: An ester is made from ethanol and propanoic acid. What is its name?
explain: The alcohol provides the first part of the name (ethyl) and the acid provides the second part (propanoate), so the ester is ethyl propanoate.

q: Which fraction of petroleum is used as jet fuel?
explain: Kerosene is used as aircraft fuel. Gasoline is the fuel for cars and diesel oil is for diesel engines.

q: A student bubbles ethane through aqueous bromine. What is observed?
explain: Ethane is a saturated alkane and does not react with aqueous bromine under these conditions, so there is no colour change.

q: Which row correctly describes condensation polymerisation?
options: one C=C per monomer | polymer only
two functional groups per monomer | polymer and a small molecule
two functional groups per monomer | polymer only
one C=C per monomer | polymer and a small molecule
explain: Condensation monomers have two functional groups, and a small molecule such as water is lost as each link forms. Addition polymerisation needs C=C and gives only the polymer.

q: What is a disadvantage of making ethanol by fermentation?
options: It is a slow batch process that gives a dilute, impure product.
It needs a very high pressure.
It uses a non-renewable raw material.
It produces a pure product that needs no further processing.
explain: Fermentation gives a dilute mixture, so the ethanol must be separated by distillation, and each batch takes days.

q: What is formed when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst?
explain: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol react to form an ester and water: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.

q: Which equation shows propene reacting with hydrogen?
explain: Hydrogen adds across the double bond to form the saturated alkane propane, CH₃CH₂CH₃. The other formulae are incorrect.

q: What can be done with PET plastic?
options: It can be cracked to form crude oil.
It can be converted back into monomers and re-polymerised.
It can be fermented to form ethanol.
It can be dissolved to form alkenes.
explain: PET can be broken down to its monomers and the monomers re-polymerised to make new PET.

q: The displayed formula of ethene shows every atom and bond. How many covalent bonds does it show, counting the double bond as two bonds?
explain: Ethene (C₂H₄) has four C–H bonds and one C=C double bond, which counts as two bonds, giving 4 + 2 = 6.

q: What is the name of the ester with the formula CH₃COOCH₃?
explain: The acid part has two carbons (ethanoate) and the alcohol part has one (methyl), so it is methyl ethanoate.

q: Which fraction of petroleum is used as a chemical feedstock?
explain: Naphtha is used as a feedstock for making many other chemicals. Refinery gas is used for heating and cooking.

q: What is a substitution reaction?
options: One atom or group of atoms is replaced by another atom or group of atoms.
Two molecules combine to form one product.
One large molecule breaks into smaller molecules.
Atoms are added across a carbon–carbon double bond.
explain: In substitution an atom or group is replaced, such as H replaced by Cl in an alkane. Addition reactions join two molecules into one product.

q: What are proteins?
options: natural polyesters made from sugar monomers
addition polymers made from alkene monomers
natural polyamides made from amino acid monomers
explain: Proteins are natural polymers with amide links, formed from amino acid monomers.

q: Why is air kept out during the fermentation of glucose to make ethanol?
options: Oxygen would make the yeast produce carbon dioxide.
Oxygen would make the glucose insoluble.
Oxygen would raise the temperature to 300 °C.
Oxygen would oxidise the ethanol to ethanoic acid.
explain: In air the ethanol is oxidised by bacteria to ethanoic acid, so the mixture would turn into vinegar.

q: Which structural formula represents the ester formed from ethanoic acid and methanol?
explain: The ester link –COO– joins the two parts: CH₃CO– from the acid and –OCH₃ from methanol, giving CH₃COOCH₃ (methyl ethanoate).

q: But-2-ene reacts with bromine. What is the structural formula of the product?
explain: One Br atom adds to each carbon of the C=C bond, giving CH₃CHBrCHBrCH₃ (2,3-dibromobutane).

q: Which row correctly describes ethene?
options: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ | contains a C=C double bond | unsaturated
CₙH₂ₙ | contains only single C–C bonds | saturated
CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ | contains only single C–C bonds | unsaturated
CₙH₂ₙ | contains a C=C double bond | unsaturated
explain: Ethene is an alkene (CₙH₂ₙ) with a C=C double bond, so it is unsaturated.

q: Ethene reacts with steam in the presence of an acid catalyst. What is the name of the product?
explain: Steam adds across the C=C bond of ethene to form ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH.

q: Which fraction of petroleum is used as a fuel for ships and for home heating systems?
explain: Fuel oil is burned in ships and in home heating systems. Lubricating oil is used for lubricants, waxes and polishes.

q: Which two functional groups does every amino acid molecule contain?
options: an amino group, –NH₂, and a carboxylic acid group, –COOH
a hydroxyl group, –OH, and an ester group, –COO–
explain: Amino acids have an –NH₂ group at one end and a –COOH group at the other. They link through these groups to make the amide bonds in a protein.

q: Which row correctly describes the reaction of methane with chlorine to form chloromethane?
options: substitution | no light needed | two products
addition | no light needed | two products
explain: Methane and chlorine undergo a photochemical substitution reaction that forms CH₃Cl and HCl.

q: Which substances can be manufactured by the cracking of larger alkane molecules?
explain: Cracking breaks alkanes into shorter alkanes, alkenes and hydrogen.

q: Which statement about nylon and protein is correct?
options: Both are made by addition polymerisation.
Both are made from alkene monomers.
explain: Nylon and proteins are polyamides made by condensation polymerisation and both have –CONH– links.

q: Which gas is also produced during the fermentation of aqueous glucose by yeast?
explain: Fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide. The carbon dioxide turns limewater milky.

q: Which gas is produced when ethanoic acid reacts with zinc?
explain: Acids react with reactive metals to produce hydrogen, which gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint.

q: Which compound is a structural isomer of but-1-ene, CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂?
explain: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ (but-2-ene) is C₄H₈ like but-1-ene but has the double bond in a different position. The others have different molecular formulae.
